newsitem.title: USA: Business groups back Calif. Governor's tax plan.
newsitem.headline: Business groups back Calif. Governor's tax plan.

text.p: California business groups on Wednesday endorsed Gov. Pete Wilson's proposal to cut state bank and corporate taxes by 10 percent, saying the governor's plan would bolster employment in the state.
The proposal, announced as part of Wilson's State of the State address on Tuesday, would phase in the tax cut by five percent each year over the next two years.
John Bryson, chairman of the California Business Roundtable, said the proposal would stimulate California's economy and create jobs.

"We are hopeful the Legislature will recognize the tremendous economic benefits this tax cut will bring Californians and encourage their support for it in the Governor's 1997-1998 budget," Bryson said.
Larry McCarthy, president of the California Taxpayers' Association, said the tax reduction would make California more competitive and would bring investment to the state.
"This economic activity, in turn, will bring higher sustainable levels of revenue to public agencies," he added.
